content.title: Single Target Escape | Dual Disaster Approach
content.summary: Keep the destination readable while collapse from behind alternates with danger ahead. One full-body recovery and one near miss provide visible proof of the subject's propulsion and control.

quick_start.input_format: Main subject + visible endpoint + closure behind + danger ahead + one full-body recovery + near-miss result demonstrating capability
quick_start.recommended_input: The maintenance drone moves toward the visible airlock, with partitions behind it closing sequentially and a mechanical arm in front sweeping across; it completes a full-body flip recovery, grazing the shield before entering the airlock.
required_anchors: Alternating dangers from front and back rather than simultaneous chaos
Near-miss results are visible and demonstrate protective capabilities
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Forward-motion sequences that alternate route closure behind the subject with new danger ahead, then use one recovery and one near miss to prove the propulsion system before a readable finish.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Keep one destination visible while a single operator advances along a constrained route. Alternate obstacles from behind, ahead and the side so each requires a different physical adaptation without changing the goal. Reserve one deliberate control action for the endpoint, then prove success with a near-miss protective state that visibly intercepts the pursuing hazard.

invariants.rule: Show the destination before the first obstacle.
invariants.ablation_failure: A hidden target turns the sequence into generic running.

invariants.rule: Alternate obstacle direction across at least three vectors.
invariants.ablation_failure: All hazards from behind produce one-note escalation.

invariants.rule: Preserve one travel direction and recover after each disruption.
invariants.ablation_failure: Direction resets make progress impossible to measure.

invariants.rule: Require a physical endpoint control action.
invariants.purpose: Lets the subject cause the outcome.

invariants.rule: Prove the control with a visible near-miss interception.
invariants.ablation_failure: A cut to safety does not show why the subject survived.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original subject or system whose identity remains stable.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One visible variable that changes in countable causal stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained behavior rule that makes the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: A coherent information order that does not copy source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: One clean physical or graphic consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: A new hierarchy of diegetic cues supporting state changes.

anti_copy_exclusions: geothermal reactor catwalk and lava eruptions
falling industrial pipes and steam jet
large wheel control and blast shield
